title: Final pytest JSON report versus incremental phase events
question: Which reporting and presentation information survives normal, parallel and interrupted execution on the selected library versions?
method: Synthetic local test sessions emit both report formats under serial, xdist, SIGINT, controller kill and worker exit conditions. A separate Typer command compares piped and TTY stderr with piped JSON stdout.
commands: uv run --isolated --no-project --python "$(readlink -f .venv/bin/python)" --with pytest==9.1.1 --with pytest-xdist==3.8.0 --with pytest-reportlog==1.0.0 --with pytest-json-report==1.5.0 --with pytest-metadata==3.1.1 --with pluggy==1.7.0 --with typer==0.28.0 --with rich==15.0.0 python docs/design_review/evidence/2026-11-18_tdm-test-reporting/probe.py

inputs.role: Synthetic cases, subprocess experiments and projection code

outputs.role: Recorded version, phase, collection, metadata and stream observations

conclusion: The probe distinguished the reporting boundaries. Normal runs supplied useful per-phase JSON, but the final report omitted session metadata, lacked a distributed collection inventory, labeled a setup-only interrupted item passed, and was absent after controller kill. Incremental reports survived. Rich rendered progress only on TTY stderr while piped stdout and the failing exit status stayed intact.
